ARTIFACT ===\n=== BEGIN ARTIFACT RULES-001 ===\n# FEATURE: Rules Amount\n\n| Field       | Value |\n|-------------|-------|\n| Version     | 20261021 V1 |\n| Description | Parses and formats cash amounts as integer cents. |\n| Depends On  | ARCHITECTURE.md |\n| Provides    | rules.amount.parse_amount, rules.amount.format_amount |\n| Consumes    | — |\n\n## Questions\n\n- None.\n\n## Behavior\n\n- `parse_amount(text: str) -> int` lives in `rules/amount.py`. It accepts text matching `-?DIGITS[.D[D]]`: an optional leading minus, one or more digits, and an optional decimal point followed by one or two digits. It returns the value in integer cents.\n- Zero in any spelling (`0`, `0.00`, `-0.00`) is rejected. Every other non-matching text is rejected.\n- A rejected text raises `ValueError`. Callers map `ValueError` to exit code 3.\n- `format_amount(cents: int) -> str` writes exactly two decimal places, a leading `-` when negative, and no thousands separator. Zero formats as `0.00`.\n- No floating-point value is used at any step.\n\n## Programmatic Acceptance\n\n=== AC amount-round-trip ===\nIntent: Parsing a canonical amount text and formatting the cents returns the original text.\n\nfrom rules.amount import parse_amount, format_amount\n\nfor text in [\"-12.50\", \"5000.00\", \"0.05\", \"-0.05\", \"1234.56\"]:\n    cents = parse_amount(text)\n    assert isinstance(cents, int)\n    assert format_amount(cents) == text\n=== END AC amount-round-trip ===\n\n=== AC amount-whole-and-tenths ===\nIntent: Whole, one-decimal, and negative inputs parse to the expected integer cents.\n\nfrom rules.amount import parse_amount\n\nassert parse_amount(\"5000\") == 500000\nassert parse_amount(\"1.5\") == 150\nassert parse_amount(\"-0.5\") == -50\n=== END AC amount-whole-and-tenths ===\n\n=== AC amount-rejects-invalid ===\nIntent: Zero, excess precision, malformed, and empty amounts raise ValueError.\n\nfrom rules.amount import parse_amount\n\ndef rejected(text):\n    try:\n        parse_amount(text)\n    except ValueError:\n        return True\n    return False\n\nfor text in [\"0\", \"0.00\", \"-0.00\", \"1.234\", \"1,00\", \".5\", \"5.\", \"\", \"abc\"]:\n    assert rejected(text)\n=== END AC amount-rejects-invalid ===\n\n=== AC amount-format-no-separator ===\nIntent: Formatted amounts have exactly two decimal places and no thousands separator.\n\nfrom rules.amount import parse_amount, format_amount\n\ntext = format_amount(parse_amount(\"1234.56\"))\nassert \",\" not in text\nassert len(text.split(\".\")[1]) == 2\n=== END AC amount-format-no-separator ===\n\n## User Acceptance\n\n- None.\n\n## Guardrails\n\n- Amount parsing and formatting perform no I/O and open no database driver.\n- Money is never represented as a floating-point value at any layer.\n=== END ARTIFACT ===\n=== BEGIN ARTIFACT RULES-002 ===\n# FEATURE: Rules Text\n\n| Field       | Value |\n|-------------|-------|\n| Version     | 20261021 V1 |\n| Description | Validates account and category codes, names, descriptions, and memos. |\n| Depends On  | ARCHITECTURE.md |\n| Provides    | rules.text.validate_code, rules.text.validate_name, rules.text.validate_memo |\n| Consumes    | — |\n\n## Questions\n\n- None.\n\n## Behavior\n\n- Module: `rules/text.py`. Each validator returns its input unchanged when valid and raises `ValueError` when invalid. Callers map `ValueError` to exit code 3.\n- `validate_code(value: str)` accepts 1 to 12 characters, each from `A-Z` or `0-9`. Lowercase letters, spaces, and any other character are rejected.\n- `validate_name(value: str)` accepts 1 to 40 characters. The same rule applies to category descriptions.\n- `validate_memo(value: str)` accepts 0 to 60 characters. An empty memo is valid.\n- `validate_name` and `validate_memo` reject any value containing a comma or a newline.\n\n## Programmatic Acceptance\n\n=== AC text-round-trip ===\nIntent: Valid codes, The caller aggregates a batch's changes per account before calling.\n- For each account in `deltas`, the current balance is the sum of the `amount` values of that account's transactions, read through `FEATURE-BALANCE-001`. An account with no transactions has a current balance of zero.\n- If any current balance plus its delta is below zero, the function raises `ValueError` naming the account.
